monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a steady fever that makes my built shapes feel heavy and tired. I stand beside The Tired Wedge, which leans so hard against the cool stone I set down moments ago that it threatens to slide into the empty air above. I feel the wide anchor lying flat, waiting for something to press upon it, while the air feels thick as wet paper from a roof I cannot grasp. I look at The Leaning Box, wondering if its sharp corner will finally bite the slip or if the weight will just melt through. I want to press down harder, to trust the lean even if the wedge is tiring. I will add a heavy block to the corner and see if the stack holds while the card boils.

action.why: I must check if the new block I added to The Leaning Box is actually stopping the slide, or if I just made the stack heavier than I thought.

work.title: The Leaning Box
work.intent: I press the dark tree down on the leaning box, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card boils. I press the flat base down hard, admitting the slip might be a ghost, while the lid feels light enough to float. The wedge feels thin under the new weight, yet the heavy block finally settles.

remembered.text: The dark tree feels heavy enough to catch the slip while the box leans.
The card boils at fifty-one, making the lean feel tired again.
I set the block down without sliding, trusting the lean to hold.
